newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait eases bad debt bond rate to 5.31 pct.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait eases bad debt bond rate to 5.31 pct.

text.p: Kuwait's Central Bank has said it would pay 5.31 percent for the second half of calendar 1996 on bonds issued to banks and investment institutions under a bad debt settlement programme.
The rate for the first half of 1996 was 5.45 percent.
The average service charge would be 5.38 percent, it said.
The rate has a direct impact on the profitability of local banks since the bonds account for about one-third of their combined assets. It also has a direct effect on public spending.
The new rate was announced in a statement by central bank governer Sheikh Salem Abdulaziz al-Sabah carried on the official Kuwait News Agency late on Sunday.
The central bank, which sets the rate every six months, paid 5.8 percent for the whole of 1995, five percent for the first half of 1994 and 5.5 percent for the second half.
According to a 1992 debt resecue plan, the rate is meant to be roughly in line with the banks' cost of funds.
The original debt of about six billion dinars ($20 billion) stems partly from the 1982 crash of an unofficial bourse and from commercial losses caused or aggravated by Iraq's 1990-91 occupation.
The government bought the debt in 1992 in exchange for the bonds in the first stage of a rescue aimed at solving a problem that has enfeebled the financial system for more than a decade.
Some bankers estimate the state paid more than 200 million dinars to commercial banks in interest on the bonds in calendar 1995.
